tweets.text:
I am okay with Kimi 3.1 deliberately leaving out top-end offensive cyber capabilities from their training data.

Discriminating against use cases is MUCH less bad than discriminating against users. And the world does need all the time it can get to prepare, harden, check old code, (properly) formally verify new code, etc before the full weight of very powerful cyber attacks is upon us.

And if this first big wave of AI risk is not handled well, then we may well get a dystopia of highly locked down models, KYC gating on everything, highly intrusive surveillance on everything, a society where you may be a second or third or fourth-class citizen in terms of model access based on your credentials and nationality.

I cloned part of Notion and Google Sheets to show you what a software factory could look like. Autonomous agents are going to be able to replicate pretty much any software (or anything they can see and interact with).

I built a simple harness to show you what I mean. You give it a URL and then it opens a real browser, clicks around, takes screenshots, inspects the DOM, and captures how the software works.

It turns those observations into a Markdown brief and hands it to a coding agent (I used the Codex SDK, with terminal access and an MCP bridge that lets the agent use the browser itself).

The original app’s JavaScript gets stripped out and the agent writes its own interaction logic. Then it opens the replica and runs the same workflows on both. Types into cells, checks formulas, opens menus. Compares text, values, and screenshots. Measures the pixel differences and keeps fixing what’s wrong until it's done!

What's fun is that you watch the original on the left, the replica on the right, and the agent working underneath. You can click on Compare and superimpose both screenshots. 

Software is going to get very easy to copy so no more excuse to ship crappy software!

Whenever you hear the word bottleneck you shouldn’t take it for granted. 

I don’t care if it’s regulatory, societal or technological.  

Ofc nothing will be instant. But society is reflexive and reactive.  

Instead of stopping at “it takes 4-7 years to get through clinical trials” you should force your brain to go multiple steps forward.  

How much of that can be sped up? 

How much pressure will society bring to the regulators if it’s clear the only impediment to curing a disease is a bureaucrat in Washington? 

How long until challenger trials start being run on random islands when AI derisks new drug candidates? 

How much faster will we reach the point where we can simulate drugs at a cellular level if AI can speed the time to solving nanotech and the ability to miniaturize cameras that we inject into the bloodstream? 

What will the millions of people who are laid off from accounting, finance, and consulting work on when their industries are nuked to zero within a year or two? 

What about the mathematicians? 

Some of you think you know it all. Oh you covered biotech as an investor for a decade and forgot more about human anatomy than I’ll ever know. 

Whoopty fucking doo. 

You are failing to understand the system level effects of commoditizing intelligence.  

Your thinking is too one dimensional.  

You don’t introduce enough vol into a thought experiment because you’re used to operating in an environment where if you do you’re branded as schizo.  

Your whole one-track life has beat your brain into submission. 

You’re an over-educated intellectual cuck.  

Force yourself to imagine. 

Because it’ll only take one motherfucker to figure out how to leverage these models properly and we’ll be off to the races.
